hypotheses.title: Coordinate prefill admission within an active expert-parallel collective group
hypotheses.mechanism: Proposed, untested adaptation: ranks that must enter the same MoE collective agree on an iteration-level prefill limit based on the slowest predicted participating rank. Each rank retains local request ownership. The group is resolved from the active backend and process groups; independent replicas decide separately.
hypotheses.nearest_prior_art: SLOWeave supplies the deadline-based chunk rule. P-PAS supplies online token-budget adaptation. FlowPrefill and fairness-aware scheduling address granularity and starvation. The earlier B200 shortlist proposed fixed cadence.
hypotheses.new_adaptation: A group-scoped admission contract would account for rank skew, collective participation, graph-compatible shapes, and KV capacity. Its absence from the historical pinned runtime is unverified.
hypotheses.code_surface: After active-backend resolution: scheduler admission and token budgeting, per-rank timing and deadline summaries, process-group coordination, graph-shape checks, KV reservation, and stale-state fallback.
hypotheses.online_policy: Observe active decode deadlines, queued prefill tokens, supported graph shapes, free KV blocks, and recent per-rank iteration and collective-wait times. Calibrate a conservative per-shape cost estimate from completed iterations, including coordination. Each group iteration selects the largest shared prefill limit whose predicted slowest-rank completion precedes the earliest reported decode deadline; ranks admit local chunks within that limit. If no chunk fits, run decode-only when feasible. Prioritize overdue decode and record misses; with no active decode, admit bounded prefill. An age threshold guarantees prefill progress while recording any deadline tradeoff. Control messages, prediction, and smaller iterations add overhead. On stale timing, coordination failure, unsupported shapes, or insufficient KV, fall back to the best qualified fixed cadence and budget. Strongest static comparator: a matched fixed-cadence and token-budget sweep.
hypotheses.strongest_objection: The central deadline rule and adaptive budgeting are prior art. The supplied participation requirement applies to a passthrough all-to-all path, while the pinned active backend is unknown. The supplied FlashInfer path already obtains cross-rank token metadata for workspace selection, so a separate admission exchange may duplicate existing coordination. Target traces may show little mixed-step rank skew, in which case coordination and smaller chunks could lose to fixed settings.

novelty.deployment: Unestablished for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on B200 in DEP8 or two DEP4 replicas.
novelty.implementation: A collective-scoped scheduling contract is proposed; its absence from the pinned runtime is unproved.
novelty.publication: Unestablished given close deadline-aware, adaptive-budget, and fairness-aware prior art.

hypotheses.confidence: Moderate mechanism plausibility; low confidence in target benefit or implementation novelty.
hypotheses.readiness: Trace gate only. Resolve the historical active backend and process groups, then require material mixed prefill/decode rank skew before implementation.

rubric.value: Possible TPOT-tail protection during mixed prefill and decode; TTFT, throughput, and cost may worsen. No target gain is established.
rubric.mechanism: Local admission under a shared limit for ranks that actually share an active collective.
rubric.evidence: Prior-art abstracts and a branch diff motivate a trace-gated test. They establish neither measured B200 transfer nor implementation absence.
rubric.integration: High until the pinned backend, process groups, graph repertoire, and scheduler contract are resolved.
rubric.correctness: Preserve request token order, required collective participation, graph and KV bounds, and output agreement at matched precision and sampling.
rubric.experiment: Check trace incidence and skew first; compare unchanged pin, tuned fixed settings, and an applicable SLOWeave-style controller.
rubric.cost: Read-only trace analysis and CPU replay precede implementation or GPU serving experiments; later cost is unknown.
rubric.distinctness: Potentially distinct group coordination. Deadline selection, adaptive budgeting, and aging are established ideas.
rubric.research_contribution: Conditional implementation adaptation; publication novelty unestablished.

experiment.control: Qualify DEP8 and two DEP4 replicas independently. At matched model, backend, precision, MTP/DSpark state, graph repertoire, KV capacity, cache preparation, request bodies, and concurrency, compare unchanged pinned behavior, a fixed cadence and budget sweep, and an applicable SLOWeave-style controller. Include the refreshed guide's DEP4 cadence only at applicable load and configuration.
experiment.treatment: The proposed collective-group policy under the same graph and memory limits.
experiment.measurements: For the approximately 8K-input/1K-output agent workload across loads: mixed-step incidence, per-rank work and collective wait, predictor error, decision overhead, graph choices, queue age, cache misses, TTFT, TPOT, throughput, cost per token, peak memory, and answer quality.
experiment.reject_if: Rank skew is immaterial; no reliable group contract exists on the active backend; prediction or coordination consumes available slack; prefill starves; or the best matched comparator meets or beats the treatment on required service and quality criteria.
experiment.correctness: Check unequal and empty rank batches under the active collective path, cancellation, cache hits and misses, graph replay, KV exhaustion, and output agreement at matched precision and sampling.
experiment.cost: Trace analysis and CPU replay first. Build, capture, serving time, and memory overhead remain unknown.
